course: Physics I - Newton's laws of motion
source_note: Concepts from the PlusOne demo pack (materials/physics1_newton), aligned with OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, Ch. 5 (CC BY 4.0). Not official PoliTO notes.

nodes.name: Force as an interaction
nodes.description: A force is a push or pull exerted BY one body ON another body. Every force has a source and a recipient.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.1 Forces; handout Core idea 3

nodes.name: Net (vector sum) force
nodes.description: The net force is the vector sum of ALL external forces on the chosen body, with directions/signs, not a single applied force.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.1, §5.3; handout Core idea 2 + worked example

nodes.name: Velocity vs acceleration
nodes.description: Velocity is how fast and in which direction a body moves; acceleration is how its velocity changes. A body can move with zero acceleration.

nodes.name: Mass and inertia
nodes.description: Mass measures inertia: how strongly a body resists changes in its velocity. More mass means less acceleration for the same net force.

nodes.name: Newton's first law
nodes.description: If the net external force on a body is zero, its acceleration is zero: it stays at rest or keeps moving at constant velocity.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.2 Newton's First Law; handout Core idea 1

nodes.name: Newton's second law
nodes.description: The net external force equals mass times acceleration (sum F = m a); acceleration points along the net force.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.3 Newton's Second Law; handout Core idea 2

nodes.name: Choosing the body / system
nodes.description: Before applying Newton's laws, choose which body or system you analyse; only forces from outside it are external forces.

nodes.name: Newton's third law (interaction pairs)
nodes.description: If A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A. The pair acts on DIFFERENT bodies, so the two forces never cancel on one body.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.5 Newton's Third Law; handout Core idea 3

nodes.name: Free-body diagram
nodes.description: Isolate one body and draw only the external forces acting on it. Velocity, acceleration or net force are not extra force arrows.
nodes.source: OpenStax UP1 §5.7 Drawing Free-Body Diagrams; handout Core idea 4

nodes.name: Weight and normal force
nodes.description: Weight (m g, downward) is the Earth's pull on the body; the normal force is the surface's push, perpendicular to the surface.

nodes.name: Static friction
nodes.description: Static friction takes whatever value from zero up to its maximum (mu_s N) is needed to prevent slipping; it is not always at its maximum.

nodes.name: Kinetic friction
nodes.description: Once surfaces slide, kinetic friction opposes the relative sliding motion between them.

nodes.name: Frictionless incline
nodes.description: On an incline, the weight splits into m g sin(theta) along the slope and m g cos(theta) perpendicular to it; frictionless: a = g sin(theta).
